chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa from Aban from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding the one in Ihram when he attains a prey, so the ransom is obligated upon him, therefore it is upon him that he should sacrifice; if it was during Hajj, at Mina where the people sacrifice; so if it was during an Umrah, he should sacrifice at Makkah. And, if he so desires, he can leave it until he proceeds (to Makkah), so he buys it, for it would suffice from him.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِم: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: Where should a pilgrim in Ihram sacrifice the hunted animal as ransom?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific geographical and procedural requirements for offering fidya (ransom) after hunting while in Ihram, distinguishing between the sacrifice sites for Hajj (Mina) and Umrah (Makkah). It reflects the Shia juristic tradition of linking the location of the sacrifice to the sanctity of the respective pilgrimage rites, while offering flexibility by allowing the hunter to retain the animal or purchase a replacement to ensure the ritual obligation is fulfilled correctly.
